title: Metal-Organic Framework Cathodes Based on a Vanadium Hexacyanoferrate Prussian Blue Analogue for High-Performance Aqueous Rechargeable Batteries

nodes.label: Stationary grid storage needs cheap, safe aqueous cells, which means a high-capacity cathode that works in water
Aqueous Prussian blue analogue cathodes have been stuck at 50-65 mA h/g
A framework in which both metal sites are redox active should give multi-electron capacity, if it can be made crystalline enough
Vanadium hexacyanoferrate as the cathode framework, so V and Fe can both cycle

attrs.reason: two redox-active metal centres, open cubic framework

nodes.label: Co-precipitation with 1 vol% HCl, so the precursor ratio stays constant and the acid slows crystal growth

attrs.reason: constant molar ratio and retarded growth give narrow size and high crystallinity

nodes.label: Three synthesis routes compared: simple mixing, co-precipitation without HCl, co-precipitation with HCl
Ex situ Fe and V K-edge XANES at held states of charge, so the two redox centres can be followed separately

attrs.reason: element-specific, and works on the amorphous fraction too

nodes.label: Co-precipitate the two solutions, hold at 60 C for 3 h, vacuum dry at 80 C and ball mill

attrs.params: 1 vol% HCl, 60 C / 3 h, 80 C vacuum

nodes.label: Galvanostatic cycling in 0.5 M Na2SO4 + H2SO4 between 0.45 and 1.15 V, 55-3520 mA/g, to 250 cycles
All three powders are the cubic V3[Fe(CN)6]2 phase (PDF 00-042-1440)
Acidified co-precipitation gives fine, narrowly distributed nanoparticles; simple mixing gives a wide size spread
Crystallinity ranks co-precipitation with HCl above without HCl above simple mixing

attrs.proxy: XRD peak sharpness and resolution of the (200)/(220) and (400)/(420) pairs

nodes.label: Take the HCl co-precipitated powder forward as the cathode
Discharge capacity 91 mA h/g at 110 mA/g, far above a single-electron PBA
Both metals change valence on charge: Fe moves up to Fe3+ and V moves up from about V4+
Two redox centres in one framework transfer more than one electron per formula unit, which is where the extra capacity comes from
Rate capability: average discharge falls only from 94 to 54 mA h/g as the current rises 64-fold
The open framework, with a lattice above 10 A and its water channels, lets guest ions move with little dehydration
Capacity decays continuously from 91 to 54 mA h/g over 250 cycles at 110 mA/g
The fade is growing charge-transfer resistance plus V and Fe dissolution, not loss of crystallinity or of particle shape
The cathode is a candidate for large-scale aqueous stationary storage
A dual-redox V/Fe framework, made crystalline by acidified co-precipitation, delivers 91 mA h/g in an aqueous cell
Prior aqueous PBAs: Cu/Fe ~55, Ni/Fe ~50-60, Cu/Ni/Fe 50-65 mA h/g
91 mA h/g is roughly half again the best previously reported aqueous PBA cathode
K-edge energy position maps to oxidation state through the FeO/Fe2O3 and V2O3/VO2/V2O5 reference spectra
Equivalent circuit Re plus a film RC element plus a charge-transfer element with Warburg tail
The edge positions never reach the V5+, V3+ or Fe2+ reference lines, so the full three-couple redox range is not demonstrated
FE-SEM: simple mixing gives aggregates with a wide size spread, both co-precipitations give finer particles, finest with HCl

notes: Lost: the Rietveld model behind the oxygen-substituted cyanide bridges, the vacancy count and the water network (STR/chemistry/bonding, dropped for budget), the FT-IR/TGA panel F1g, the EDS maps F1h, the dQ/dV analysis, and the 880/1760 mA/g long-cycling figure, which MatMech records as figure '?' and which the packet does not carry. Three audits: HRTEM still shows amorphous regions in the best powder (o4); the XANES edge positions never reach the V5+, V3+ or Fe2+ reference lines, so the claimed V3+/V4+/V5+ and Fe2+/Fe3+ couples are only partly shown (o9, n28); and the Nyquist plots carry no resolved charge-transfer arc while the fitted Rct keeps rising to cycle 250 instead of saturating after cycle 30 as the text says (o12). The panel that is in the packet shows capacity falling from 91 to 54 mA h/g over 250 cycles, i.e. ~59% retention, not the 80% the MatMech summary quotes for a different current density. Packet defect: packet F5 carries the paper's Figure 6 caption, so the F-ids are offset and the paper's Figure 5 is absent.

changes: Added n12 -motivates-> n14. The down_select had only o5 (an OBS) as a parent, so it was a second spine root; n12 is the ranking claim (crystallinity HCl > no HCl > simple mixing) that the choice is made on, which is the screen-then-choose use of motivates.

n21 (MEC/identification of the fade) set spine=false: it was a third spine root with no incoming spine edge, and adding one would have made a two-cycle with n21 -explains-> n20. It stays as a side claim explaining n20 and supporting n23. Spine 20 -> 19, and the spine now has two parallel property branches (capacity/rate) plus the fade, not three roots.

panel_checks.note: F1f is the HRTEM of the HCl powder, 5 nm scale bar, with red arrows on lattice-fringed domains and white arrows on featureless regions. The arrowed amorphous regions do occupy a share of the field comparable to the fringed ones, so the audit against 'high crystallinity' is fair.

F3d plots Fe and V edge energies against normalised charge capacity with dashed Fe3+/Fe2+ and V5+/V4+/V3+ reference lines. Fe runs ~7124.5 to ~7126.3 eV, arriving on the Fe3+ line; V runs ~5469.75 to ~5470.5 eV, crossing the V4+ line and stopping short of V5+ at 5471.0. The Fe2+, V3+ and V5+ lines are never reached, which is exactly the n28 limitation.

F5d shows Re, Rfilm and Rct against cycle number: Rct rises from ~3 to ~28 ohm with error bars of several ohm and is still rising at cycle 250 (with a dip at 200), while Rfilm sits near 2.5-3 and Re near 0.3. The node's reading, and its audit that the text's 'saturates after cycle 30' is not what the panel shows, both hold.

review.audit_summary: Three audits (o4, o9/n28, o12), at budget and each one changing support. They are correctly graded rather than lumped together: o4 and o9 are 'the figure does not resolve the full claim' (the best powder still has amorphous regions; the edge positions never reach three of the five reference lines), and both are attached with qualifies edges to nodes that keep their other evidence. o12 is the strongest and is the one genuine figure-against-text conflict - the Nyquist plots carry no resolved charge-transfer arc, and the fitted Rct keeps climbing where the text says it saturates - and it is carried by image_support=partial plus an explicit image_note rather than being dressed up as a contradiction. The notes also record that the packet's panel shows ~59% retention over 250 cycles against the 80% in the MatMech summary block, which r04 ruling #37 says to resolve in favour of the figure.
